title: Predict, then measure
brief: Write the roofline, wave-quantization, and Little's-law predictors, then compare them with the measured time of kernels whose arithmetic intensity you can tune, and report the measured ridge point.
hints: The first run compiles three CUDA kernels with nvcc, which takes 30 to 60 seconds. Later runs reuse the cached build.
Roofline time is the larger of two times: FLOPs divided by the peak rate, and bytes divided by the bandwidth. Convert TFLOP/s and GB/s to FLOP/s and byte/s before you divide.
A kernel that does k FMAs per element does 2*k FLOPs per element and moves 8 bytes per element: it reads 4 and writes 4.
Waves are a ceiling division: ceil(num_blocks / (blocks_per_sm * sm_count)). Efficiency is num_blocks divided by waves times the capacity of one wave.
Little's law: bytes in flight equals bandwidth times latency. Convert the latency from cycles to seconds with the clock in MHz first.
For measured_ridge, take the highest FLOP/s any kernel reached and the highest byte rate any kernel reached. Their ratio is the measured ridge point.
